subject: Discovery: MediaPulse logging & PII handling
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: MediaPulse logging & PII handling

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking 30 minutes today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points you shared
- Chat transcripts contain customer PII (emails, phone numbers, partial card info) and are currently logged to your analytics pipeline.
- Token billing spikes because full transcripts are sent to our hosted model endpoints; you want to reduce cost without losing observability.
- Audit/forensics needs: security team needs immutable access logs and the ability to produce redacted transcripts for compliance reviews.
- Retention constraints: legal requires most logs be purged within 30 days; some anonymous metrics can be retained longer.

Current stack (from your notes)
- Frontend chat -> internal API layer -> Kafka -> analytics + call to LLM endpoint (hosted).
- Logs live in S3 (30–90 day lifecycle) and consumer dashboards in Snowflake.

Success criteria you mentioned
- Ability to redact PII at ingestion (configurable rules) OR deliver automatic redaction before persistent storage.
- Configurable retention windows per data-class (PII: 30d; anonymized events: 180d).
- Proof points for auditability (signed access logs, exportable audit trail) for SOC2 readiness.
- Minimal latency impact to chat experience (<150ms added on average).

What Redwood can do (high level)
- Prefix/KV caching + selective logging so only hashes or token counts are stored for sensitive routes.
- On-request redaction hooks and deterministic regex-based redactors at the API gateway (we can also run redaction in your VPC for extra isolation).
- Retention policies per route/model with automated purge jobs and retention logs.
- Audit logs that include request metadata (timestamp, route, model version, user-id hash) and optional request/response digests for forensic verification.

Immediate next steps
1) Tech deep-dive: 60m session with your infra/security (suggest Tue 7/21) to go over redaction placement and log schema.
2) I will send a short redaction/retention checklist and an example retention lifecycle we use for customers.
3) We’ll provide an initial scoped POC plan (30 days) that isolates PII flows and demonstrates retention+audit exports.

Attachments: data-retention-checklist.xlsx (skeleton), redaction-faq.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times for the deep-dive and drop the checklist into the shared Drive link below.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
https://redwoodinference.com
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@mediapulse.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery: MediaPulse logging & PII handling

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the clear recap — that looks accurate. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- Retention: Legal is strict about PII being removed from persistent storage at 30 days, but security would like a 90-day window for raw logs if we can keep them in an encrypted, access-controlled staging area (we know this may be difficult).
- Redaction: We prefer redaction-as-close-to-source-as-possible (at the frontend/API gateway) to avoid sending raw PII to any external service.
- Audit: We need an exportable CSV of access events for at least 12 months (not the full transcripts, just metadata) and the ability to produce redacted transcripts on demand for compliance reviews.

On participants: I’m looping in our CTO alias (cto@mediapulse.com) to confirm feasibility of the front-line redaction approach.

Available times for the deep-dive: Tue 7/21 after 10am EST or Wed 7/22 morning.

Appreciate it — Jane

Jane Doe
Director, Product Operations | MediaPulse
jane.doe@mediapulse.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: MediaPulse logging & PII handling

Jane — perfect, thanks for the specifics. Quick replies inline and next steps.

Retention: 30-day purge for PII is straightforward; we can support an encrypted staging bucket kept for 90 days with stricter IAM + audit triggers if you want to pursue that model. We’ll call that an option in the POC.

Redaction placement: Agreed that frontend/API gateway redaction is preferred. We can ship a lightweight redactor (open-source rule set) that runs in your VPC or as a middleware at the edge before tokens are sent to the model. That keeps PII out of hosted endpoints entirely.

Audit exports: We can produce CSV exports for access events (user-hash, timestamp, route, model-version, action) and retain those metadata records for 12 months; the POC will demonstrate the export process.

Latency: Our edge redactor adds ~30–70ms in our benchmarks; we’ll validate with your payloads in the tech deep-dive.

Proposed immediate schedule
- Tech deep-dive (60m): Tue 2026-07-21 at 10:30am EST — invite to follow.
- I’ll drop the redaction/retention checklist to the Drive link and share a draft POC statement of work by EOD Wed 7/22.

Files: attached data-retention-checklist.xlsx and redaction-faq.pdf. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8234

If the CT O wants to join the deep-dive, Rafael (cc’d) will lead the runtime/architecture part and Marissa will cover contract/POC terms.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

—
